key_insight: PACE-ECG used patient-aware pretraining to outperform DeepECG-SSL on mortality and heart failure prediction across healthcare systems with a 41-fold smaller encoder.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest ECG representations could support transferable post-myocardial-infarction risk prediction, but do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Contrastively paired temporally neighbouring ECGs from the same patient.
Combined patient-temporal learning with clinically guided multitask supervision.
Evaluated frozen representations against DeepECG-SSL and two control baselines.
evidence_signal: Across MIMIC-IV and two external HEEDB cohorts, reported AUROC gains over DeepECG-SSL ranged from 1.9% to 6.9% for mortality and 4.0% to 11.0% for incident heart failure.
watch_item: Retrospective cross-cohort discrimination does not establish prospective clinical utility; calibration and workflow impact require further evaluation.
paper_title: PACE-ECG: Patient-Aware Contrastive ECG Pretraining; Leveraging Longitudinal Structure for Transferable Representations
